drafted_from: tool:catalog-a-channels-videos-by-format's row in tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/tool-rows.json, its script in tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/do-work/ and the tests in tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/test/
start_here: Say to your AI: "Catalog the lighthouse channel's videos by format from my YouTube folder into the show folder." It runs tool:catalog-a-channels-videos-by-format, which labels each video episode, extra, short or side and compares its views with its neighbours.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: it reads one settings row of yours (record:setting:measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging~<scope_kind>~<scope_id>) or the settings you pass, and works on files in the show's folder.
instructions: 1. Make the show's folder and the YouTube library folder the run may change, and put the yt-dlp flat lists lighthouse-videos.json and lighthouse-shorts.json in <youtube folder>/flat/. Put the keys the row needs (series_prefixes, compilation_words, side_pattern) in your settings row or pass them as settings.

2. Say the sentence in start_here to your AI. It calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:catalog-a-channels-videos-by-format and the input in the worked example; the door asks for the granted folder.
3. Read the last line it prints, {"result": ...}, or {"error": ...} saying what to fix (a missing settings key is named).
4. The catalog.tsv it wrote is the table every other tool of this folder reads (find-when-a-character-speaks, list-what-a-character-says, sum-a-characters-time-per-video); run those next.

worked_examples.title: Four videos catalogued
worked_examples.given: From the sample run in tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/tool-rows.json and CatalogTest in tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/test/test_measures.py: lighthouse-videos.json holds vid-a "The Lighthouse Hour: Fog" (1800 s, 1000 views), vid-b "Behind the lamp: tools" (600 s, 500 views) and vid-c "The Lighthouse Hour: Gulls" (1700 s, 3000 views); lighthouse-shorts.json holds clip-a "Parrot!" (20 s, 50 views).
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result": {"catalog": "{grant:change-a-folder}/show/catalog.tsv", "videos": 4}}; catalog.tsv has vid-a episode, vid-b extra (its title starts with "behind the lamp"), vid-c episode (3000 views against a baseline of 1000, x_baseline 3.0) and clip-a short.
